patch.value: Parallel jobs must not replace the shared global npm

Deep and release workflows install the pinned npm globally after setup-node. On the shared local runners every container on a host shares the toolcache Node installation, so parallel jobs replace the same npm and fail with ENOTEMPTY or npm: command not found. GitHub issue unbraind/pm-ops#284.

Every workflow installs the pinned npm with --prefix into a job-local directory and prepends its bin to the job path, keeping the exact-version assertion; A workflow-contract test fails if any workflow replaces the global npm; A regression test runs two overlapping pinned installs into separate prefixes against one shared Node directory and proves both stay at the pin with the shared npm untouched

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Root cause confirmed in the workflow source: global installation of the pinned npm replaces the same Node installation used by parallel jobs on a shared toolcache. Replaced each bootstrap with a job-local prefix, published only its bin directory to the job PATH, and retained exact-pin checks including a separate subsequent-step assertion. Workflow contracts reject global npm replacement across all workflow files. No runner settings or shared tool installations were modified.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Additional regression evidence: install processes must have overlapping lifetimes; both cold and warm rounds share a private package cache; each prefix reports the exact pin and reaches a clean npm ci. The unchanged-shared-installation check hashes every file in the shared npm package as well as checking the CLI timestamp and version. Windows uses the same prefix form with Git Bash path conversion; global npm replacement is no longer an allowed bootstrap exception.
